newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM calls for controls on finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM calls for controls on finance firms.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Wednesday called for tighter regulatory controls over finance firms after CRB Capital Markets Ltd was charged with financial irregularities, an official spokesman said.
"The prime minister had a meeting with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Finance Ministry officials to review the collapse of CRB Capital Markets," the spokesman told a news conference.

"He urged the officials to take steps to protect the interests of common investors. He also asked the officials to take legal remedies and evolve a corrective mechanism to prevent recurrence of such trends," the spokesman said.

The CBI last week said it would complete within a month an investigation into the failed CRB group of companies, accused of irregularities in financial services and whose liabilities are estimated at 9.32 billion rupees ($260 million).
Industry officials have reported growing requests for refunds from non-bank finance companies by small investors, shaken by the CRB fiasco.
"The prime minister also asked Finance Ministry officials to evolve a depositors insurance scheme covering non-bank finance companies and other companies," the spokesman said.

"The prime minister desired that those responsible for the collapse of CRB Capital Markets should be brought to book. Certain banking companies should not be in a position to defraud thousands of people," he said.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the country's central bank, last month charged the group's flagship CRB Capital Markets, which has offices in India and abroad, with a series of irregularities relating to its activities.

The bank also invited claims from investors of CRB Capital Markets for submission to the official liquidator appointed by the Delhi High Court. A winding up petition filed by the Reserve Bank of India will be heard on July 22.

The State Bank of India had lodged a complaint with the CBI against the company after it discovered the firm was defaulting on repayments and had withdrawn 580 million rupees on a loan facility, the government said in a statement on Wednesday.

It said the government had asked the RBI and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the country's stock market watchdog, to undertake a thorough review of regulatory action taken against other companies in the CRB group.
The RBI, SEBI and CBI had also formed a panel to ensure concerted action was taken, the statement said. The central bank had issued a notice to banks on procedural safeguards to be followed, it said.
The statement said authorities were searching for CRB Capital Markets' promoter, C.R. Bhansali. ($1=35.8 rupees)
